authorization: AJ via VERA card t601s2471, Nov 11 2026 1:10 America/Edmonton (UTC-6): 'FORGE, CPU only, (1) generates a larger pre-registered Y72 held-out set of about 400+ segments with the existing generator and seed policy ...'
purpose: The 200-segment Y72 held-out set has single-checkpoint SD ~5.2-5.7 segments (2.6-2.8 pp) and cannot resolve differences smaller than ~7 pp (single checkpoint) / ~4-5 pp (mean of 3). A fresh 600-segment set (never inspected before this registration) lowers the floor and, being unseen, is free of the selection that comes from having looked at the 200-set while diagnosing the drop.

generator.how_used: make_corpus_Y.py functions filler_for/piece_len/copies_for/build_needle_body/gen_rows and their constants are extracted verbatim by AST and exec'd (nothing re-implemented); distance 72, 40 rows per call, same call signature gen_rows(72, 40, seed, tag) as the original makes for the shipped 40 unseen rows
generator.leakage_policy: original BANNED (probe_Q, T2/V/W/X payloads, corpus train/valid byte blobs, running used-set) EXTENDED with every train_Y.pt payload (all geometries train+unseen, gap probes) and the 40 rehearsal rows' payloads; banned counts {"probe_Q": 869, "train_T2.pt": 720, "train_V.pt": 720, "train_W.pt": 1600, "train_X.pt": 1360, "train_Y.pt(all geometries + gaps)": 5160, "rehearsal_Y72_40 (decoded from rows)": 200}

seed_policy.original: seed = base + distance; bases train 20261500, unseen 20261600, gap 20261700; rehearsal added rows 20262672 (=20261672+1000)
seed_policy.note: each new seed is one 40-row gen_rows call = one block of 200 segments; blocks are kept so cluster/block analyses are possible

set.canonical_definition: sha256(rows int16 little-endian bytes + mask int16 little-endian bytes)
set.reproducibility: regenerating from the seeds in a second process gave the identical canonical sha256, payload-list sha256 and file sha256 (prereg/y72_heldout_v2/gen_y72_heldout_repeat.log; gen_info.json 'pt_save_deterministic' false only compares two saves inside ONE process)

overlap_check.positive_control: prereg/y72_heldout_v2/overlap_positive_control.log: injecting ONE shipped held-out row makes the checker fail (1 exact-row match, 5 payload matches)

noise_math.assumption: iterate/sampling noise is item-level (independent across segments): OBSERVED ICC by row -0.015 -> design effect 1 in the 200-item study, so SD in segments scales with sqrt(n) and SD in pp with 1/sqrt(n). A checkpoint-level component shared by all items would NOT shrink; that is the thing the scoring of existing checkpoints on the new set tests (prediction made BEFORE scoring).

gate.statement: Y72 retention on THIS set: R = (sum over checkpoints 250, 275, 300 of segments_exact >= 1440 of 1800, i.e. mean >= 480/600 = 80.0%) AND (every checkpoint >= 432/600 = 72.0%)
gate.rescaling: thresholds are percentages, unchanged from prereg/pertask_clip_v1.json (200-set: sum >= 480 of 600 evaluations, guard >= 144/200); counts scale by k = 3: 480*3 = 1440, 144*3 = 432. Only the noise shrinks: sd in pp falls by 1/sqrt(3).
gate.arithmetic: integer: sum*1000 >= 3*800*600 and count*1000 >= 720*600; no float; strict >=
gate.superseding: replaces ONLY the Y72 R gate of pertask_clip_v1 / y72fix_lambda05 for future experiments; A and N gates and verdict structure unchanged; the legacy 200-segment set remains available for comparison only and is never pooled into this gate

scoring_plan_existing_checkpoints_nongat.purpose: estimate the new set's noise floor and test the sqrt(n) scaling prediction above; results cannot change this registration (a revision would need a new rule_id and a new commit)
scoring_plan_existing_checkpoints_nongat.fail_closed: checkpoint file sha256 must equal the pinned value (from the earlier runs' ARTIFACTS.sha256) BEFORE torch.load; set file sha256 and canonical sha256 verified before scoring
statistics: per-checkpoint segment-exact on 600 and per block of 200
within-item Bernoulli SD, churn-model SD, binomial SD
row ICC and cluster bootstrap over 120 rows (seed 20261111, B=20000)
mean-of-3 SE (cluster bootstrap) and its ratio to the single-checkpoint SE

caveats: 600 segments are drawn by the same generator as the 200 (same distribution); any difficulty difference between sets is itself informative and not corrected
the sqrt(n) scaling assumes noise is item-level; a model-level component shared across items would not shrink
a single run on this set still has one seed
